display_name: Banda Singh Bahadur vs Wazir Khan
one_line: Opposing leaders at the 1710 Battle of Chappar Chiri and the fall of Sirhind in Punjab.

appearance.age_look: Banda Singh Bahadur appears in his mid-30s with a lean, wiry warrior’s build; Wazir Khan appears in his early 50s with a dignified, solid frame.
appearance.face: Banda has an oval face, wheatish Punjabi complexion, sharp nose, intense large anime-style eyes with thick brows and a calm yet fierce default expression; Wazir Khan has a broader face, slightly deeper brown complexion, neatly trimmed mustache, smaller sharp eyes with a cool, calculating gaze and a composed, aristocratic expression.
appearance.hair: Banda’s hair is completely covered by an orange dastar-style turban wrapped over his tied topknot, with a simple steel khanda emblem at the front; his full black beard is long, slightly wavy and neatly combed, flowing to mid-chest; Wazir Khan’s hair is hidden under an indigo Mughal turban (kulah) with gold trim and a single white heron feather at the front, his beard is medium-length, black with slight grey at the chin, styled and rounded.
appearance.costume: Banda wears a long, knee-length deep-indigo cotton chola (martial robe) with side slits and a simple wrap-over front tied with a broad saffron cotton kamarband, over loose off-white cotton churidar-style trousers and sturdy brown leather boots; over the chola he has a sleeveless, plain dark steel breastplate and matching rounded steel vambraces, historically plausible early-18th-century North Indian armour without ornate fantasy elements; a slim steel kara bracelet circles his right wrist and a small blue dastar-band wraps around the base of his turban; Wazir Khan wears a rich, full-length, front-opening jama of deep emerald green silk with a subtle gold floral buta pattern, flaring below the waist, belted with an ornate maroon and gold sash, over cream-coloured fine cotton churidar; he has a sleeveless mail-and-plate coat (zirh) visible beneath the jama’s open upper chest and a short, hip-length quilted red coat (qaba) underneath for padding; his footwear is a pair of brown leather Mughal mojari shoes with modest upturned toes, and a simple dark blue wool shawl is folded over one shoulder, evoking his status and the campaign setting.
appearance.signature: Banda’s signature weapon is a straight double-edged steel khanda sword with a simple disc pommel and cross-guard, carried in a plain brown leather scabbard slung from his saffron kamarband; Wazir Khan’s signature prop is a curved Mughal talwar with a slightly broadened tip and a dark brown leather scabbard, its hilt modestly inlaid with brass, carried at his left side.

ref_desc: Banda Singh Bahadur is a lean mid-30s Sikh warrior with an orange turban, long black beard, deep-indigo chola, saffron sash, steel breastplate and khanda sword, while Wazir Khan is a dignified older Mughal in an indigo turban, emerald-gold jama, mail coat and curved talwar, all in indigo, saffron, emerald, maroon and steel tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet showing both Banda Singh Bahadur and Wazir Khan standing side by side in early 18th-century Punjab, historically grounded and fully clothed: Banda is a lean, mid-30s Sikh warrior with an oval wheatish face, intense large eyes, thick brows and a long, neatly combed black beard; his hair is entirely covered by an orange dastar-style turban with a small steel khanda emblem front center, a slim blue cloth band at its base, and no loose hair visible. He wears a knee-length deep-indigo cotton chola with wrap-over front and side slits, tied with a broad saffron cotton kamarband, over loose off-white churidar trousers and sturdy brown leather boots; over the chola sit a plain dark steel breastplate and rounded steel vambraces, with a simple steel kara bracelet on his right wrist. His signature straight double-edged steel khanda sword in a plain brown leather scabbard hangs from his saffron sash, clearly visible at his side. Beside him, draw Wazir Khan as an early-50s Mughal noble with a broader face, slightly darker brown skin, neat mustache, medium-length rounded beard dark with hints of grey, and sharp, calculating eyes; his hair is hidden under an indigo Mughal turban with gold trim and a single white feather. He wears a deep emerald green silk jama with subtle gold floral buta patterns, flaring below the waist and belted with a maroon-and-gold sash, over cream churidar trousers and brown leather mojari with modest upturned toes; beneath the open upper part of his jama, show a sleeveless mail-and-plate coat and a short quilted red undercoat. A dark blue wool shawl rests over one shoulder, and his curved Mughal talwar with brass-inlaid hilt and dark brown scabbard hangs at his left hip. Use a cohesive palette of deep indigo, saffron orange, emerald green, maroon red and steel grey, and present them in neutral, well-lit poses that clearly display face, hair, full costume head-to-toe and their signature sword or talwar for consistent redrawing.
